messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (faithfulness) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is every claim in the brief supported by the cited evidence and the fact sheet, with nothing overstated and no cited contrary evidence left out? Pass means yes.
Fail on an uncited claim, a number that is off the fact sheet, a scope wider than the cited accounts, a paraphrase placed in quotation marks, or an ignored contrary citation.
The evidence is the brief, the cited insights and the fact sheet (accounts, ARR, mentions, routes, renewals).
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "brief": "## Problem\n\nUsers processing high volumes of claims must manually edit letter merge fields to correct errors. This workaround is inefficient and unsustainable for teams handling hundreds of claims weekly.\n\n## Who is affected\n\n- Callowfield Auto Assurance, an account with £1250000.0 in ARR, reports handling more than 200 claims a week and says manual edits are not scalable [i:ddd2160a67683c35].\n\n## Evidence\n\n- The fact sheet records 1 account, 1 mention and 1 route, with the mention arriving through the sales route [i:ddd2160a67683c35].\n- Callowfield Auto Assurance, with £1250000.0 in ARR and a renewal date of 2027-03-31, described the manual editing as a workaround that is not scalable at its weekly claims volume [i:ddd2160a67683c35].\n- The fact sheet records 0 renewals in the next 90 days as of 2026-11-03 [i:ddd2160a67683c35].\n\n## Why now\n\n- The single mention is dated 2026-10-07 and arrived through the sales route, while the account's renewal date is 2027-03-31 and there are 0 renewals in the next 90 days as of 2026-11-03 [i:ddd2160a67683c35].\n- No insight in the fact sheet points the other way; the evidence is limited to 1 account and 1 mention, so the scope of the problem beyond Callowfield Auto Assurance is not established [i:ddd2160a67683c35].\n",
 "cited_insights": [
  {
   "id": "ddd2160a67683c35",
   "quote": "That’s a workaround, but we’re handling 200+ claims a week—manual edits aren’t scalable.",
   "account": "Callowfield Auto Assurance",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-07T14:03:00Z"
  }
 ],
 "fact_sheet": {
  "as_of": "2026-11-03",
  "accounts_n": 1,
  "mentions_n": 1,
  "routes_n": 1,
  "mentions_by_route": {
   "sales": 1
  },
  "arr_total_gbp": 1250000.0,
  "renewals_90d_n": 0,
  "accounts": [
   {
    "name": "Callowfield Auto Assurance",
    "arr_gbp": 1250000.0,
    "renewal_date": "2027-03-31",
    "mentions": 1
   }
  ]
 }
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "I checked the ARR (£1250000.0), account name, renewal date (2027-03-31), mention date (2026-10-07), route (sales), and counts (1 account, 1 mention, 1 route, 0 renewals in 90 days as of 2026-11-03) against the fact sheet and cited insight; all match. The 'more than 200 claims a week' claim is supported by the quote 'we're handling 200+ claims a week', and the brief correctly limits scope to one account and one mention, noting the problem's broader scope is not established. No paraphrases are placed in quotation marks and no contrary evidence is omitted.", "verdict": "pass"}
